The cathode is NMC 811. 

According to the paper, at a 6C charging rate, the NMC 811 cathode with an areal loading of 2.2 mA h/cm^2 maintained 80% capacity, whereas the corresponding NMC 532 and NMC 622 cathodes with areal loadings of 2.4 mA h/cm^2 only retained 49% and 56% capacity, respectively.

If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so. The documents are pages of "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries".

expect: NMC 811 (Table 1 'Section 6 – Low-Co/Ni-Rich Cathodes (i.e. NMC 811)', a wrapped cell); 80% at 6C (2.2 mAh/cm^2) vs 49% and 56% for NMC 532 and NMC 622 (2.4 mAh/cm^2) (p7.L78-81)
question: Which cathode does Table 1's Section 6 row name, and at a 6C charging rate, what capacity did that cathode keep compared with NMC 532 and NMC 622 in the ORNL study the paper describes?
